## Context / Problem
A local `make verify` on the comment-only Group10 candidate `523a3163835c2a83175e95551595592f4b62abc0` failed `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py::test_ref_backend_acquire_release_roundtrip`. Its isolated temporary repository's `git update-ref refs/reconciler/lock` exceeded `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 5.0` and raised `RefLockTimeoutError`. The suite had 2 failures, 19,710 passes and 93 skips in 8199.03 seconds while 4 full suites were concurrent. Group10 changed only 35 infrastructure comment paths; neither this test nor `_ref_lock.py` changed.

A controlled exact-node run on byte-identical bot-identity tree `2a12fbc2badebca8c3d33e6bb4c06c66af5b1532` passed with `pytest -q -n 2` while 2 full suites were concurrent (paired with the other failed node: 2/2 in 77.21 seconds). Nonreproduction does not establish the cause.

## Reproduction (2026-10-25, current main, deterministic, no load)
Scratch copy of `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py` whose `git` shim sleeps before any `update-ref` and then delegates to real git:
- delay 1 s and 4.5 s: `test_ref_backend_acquire_release_roundtrip` passes.
- delay 5.6 s: fails with `RefLockTimeoutError: git update-ref refs/reconciler/lock timed out after 5.0s (fail-closed: treat as HELD)`, the reported error.
So the test fails whenever one local `git update-ref` in its temp repo exceeds the production bound `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (5.0 s), whatever the cause. Not reproduced: the original slow call (the failed run had 4 concurrent suites and no trace); the cause of that delay is unknown.

## Root cause
The test exercises lock semantics (acquire returns the ref oid, no tickets-branch file, release deletes the ref) but runs real git under the production fail-closed bound. A starved host can push one call past 5 s, and the lock then correctly reports "held". The production behaviour is right; the test depends on wall-clock headroom it does not control. The bound is a safety policy and must not be loosened in production.

## Decision
Keep the production bound at 5.0 s and its fail-closed meaning. In the test environment only, give the happy-path lock tests a 60 s local bound so host starvation cannot fail an assertion about lock semantics. This does loosen a time bound, in test code only, so it is recorded here and on the ticket. The fail-closed contract stays proven independently of the real bound by `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py::test_timeout_raises_reflocktimeout`, which forces a `TimeoutExpired`.

## Approach
1. In `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py`, in the existing `_ref_backend` fixture (shared by the module's ref-lock tests, not autouse), add `monkeypatch.setattr(advisory_lock._load_ref_lock(), "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS", 60.0)`. `monkeypatch` restores the production value after each test.
2. Add a test in the same module that, with the fixture applied, delays `update-ref` by 5.6 s through a PATH shim and asserts acquire and release still succeed. It takes about 12 s, which is the cost of proving the headroom, and is marked slow only if the repo already has such a marker for tests of that length.
3. Change no production code.

## Scope
In scope: `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py`. Out of scope: `_ref_lock.py`, the other ref-lock test modules that run real git under the same bound (a follow-up if they fail), and the 30 s remote bound.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py -q
make verify
```
The new delayed test must fail on main (the 5.6 s delay raises the timeout) and pass with the fixture change. The unchanged `test_timeout_raises_reflocktimeout` must still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The roundtrip test passes with `update-ref` delayed 5.6 s, where it fails on main with the reported `RefLockTimeoutError` (checked: new delayed test, which fails on main).
- [x] The fail-closed timeout test passes unchanged and no production code changed (checked: `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py -q`; diff touches only the test file).
- [x] The loosened test bound is documented in the fixture and on this ticket (checked: fixture comment; ticket comment at close).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).
